The world is getting more of its electricity from renewables but less from nuclear power.

If the world is to reduce its carbon emissions and tackle climate change, it needs to move away from fossil fuels to low-carbon power.

There are two key sources of low-carbon electricity: renewables — which include solar, wind, hydropower and others — and nuclear power.

While rapid growth in solar and wind has increased the amount of electricity coming from renewables, a lack of enthusiasm for nuclear means it’s playing a shrinking role in the global mix.

In the chart, you can see the share of global electricity coming from fossil fuels, renewables, and nuclear since 1985. Since 2000, nuclear and renewables have followed very different trajectories. Back then, both accounted for a similar share of global electricity. But in 2025, renewables made up more than three times as much: 34% compared to 9%.

The total amount of electricity produced by nuclear plants is about the same as it was two decades ago. But because the world produces much more electricity overall, its share of the electricity mix has declined.

(written by @_HannahRitchie and @parriagadap)

Because I collaborate on papers with some students, I've heard them complaining about how tough the job market is this year. I can confirm that's the reality. In my view, getting into the core teams at top companies, and by that I mean the ones where it's truly the core group of under thirty people, is exceptionally difficult not just for new graduates, but for experienced hires as well. 

Unless you have an elite school background, or a senior lab mate who already works there and might land you an interview, it's a monumental challenge. And honestly, I think that's normal. 

It's pretty clear the industry doesn't need any more meaningless innovation. When you just take A, B, C, and D and mix and match them for permutations and combinations, you can generate endless "innovations." That's why I rarely read papers these days. Truly solid work requires massive GPU compute to validate. 

Like I always say, when your work is actually deployed by manufacturers in large-scale production experiments, that's when it's genuinely recognized.

Aside: students, whether lab interns or new grads, have almost zero experience with distributed training, especially when it comes to deep distributed training frameworks like Megatron. They can usually get an experiment to run using some recipe, but they never look at metrics like MFU utilization. In industry, that translates directly to wasted money.

So having hands-on experience with this, even on a thousand-card cluster, let alone ten thousand, is a huge asset, assuming you come from a top-tier lab or have standout internship experience. Frankly, I haven't seen an intern yet who's truly fluent in distributed systems unless they come from an infra background.

I didn’t notice anyone diving in deep into this new $NBIS credit facility, so here’s exactly the mechanics of the said bridge loan that is very creative capital engineering from $NBIS All the while the rest of the AI cloud and neocloud space is getting crushed by high financing costs, balance sheet anxiety & sudden tight capital markets

 $NBIS just pulled off a $3.5B senior secured credit facility with Citi. First off accessing this level of institutional liquidity  without needing any immediate asset level contracts locked up is to me a a massive win that separates $NBIS from it's peers who is currently dragging $NBIS down. Let's dive deep in to how exactly this credit facility work, why management chose this structure and what the end game looks like.

1/ How the 364 day "credit line" work:
This isn't an amortizing loan where $NBIS starts dumping principal cash right away. It functions as a flexible bridge credit line. They draw funds as needed to build data centers and procure GPUs. The entire $3.5B principal sits as a hard lump-sum deadline at the end of the 364 days.   

2/ The 90 day step up pricing structure
The baseline interest starts at Term SOFR + 2.75%. To prevent $NBIS from treating this short term bank facility as permanent capital, Citi built in a step up penalty. Every 90 days  the borrowing margin ticks up by 25 bps until it caps out at SOFR + 3.50%. Still $NBIS has the flexibility to prepay and exit the loan at any time with zero prepayment penalty.   

3/ Why would $NBIS takes on short term bridge debt all of a sudden right now?
 Right now speed of bringing compute online is everything. Demand is scaling so fast that the return on getting physical clusters online immediately far outpaces a temporary ~3.5% spread over SOFR. Rather than spending 6 to 12 months negotiating slow, complex project finance debt up front, $NBIS takes rapid bank liquidity to capture hardware immediately which now has absurdly low payback periods. (Short term spot between 6 months - 1 year)

4/ The sequencing plan
Management explicitly calls this "sequencing" capital. First, they use the $3.5B Citi bridge line to acquire GPUs and bring up clusters. Second, they attach these active sites to their pipeline of long term hyperscaler contracts (backed by over $40B in deal interest with $35B of that non optional). Once the sites are operational and cash flowing, $NBIS swaps out this bridge facility for long term, even lower cost asset backed securities (ABS) before the 364 day clock expires.   

Bottom line: Thus this would have a near 0 impact on the balance sheet. It's an aggressive tactical play to capture market share today where the demand is beyond absurd.

荷蘭封裝設備商 Besi 這週交出第三季：訂單 3.426 億歐元，年增 96%，比市場預估多了一成五。
股價呢？從 6 月高點到現在，大約腰斬。
再往前一週，台積電法說。7 月魏哲家說，封裝緊到「已經在限制客戶成長」。10/15 被問到跟格芯的合作，他說後段「有一點短缺」。
所以很多人的結論是：封裝的戲演完了，CoWoS 不缺了。
我看完這兩週的公告，想法剛好反過來。缺口還在，只是有人先付了錢，把它排到後面幾年。
從「瓶頸」到「有一點」，中間發生什麼事
10/8，格芯公告跟台積電簽了 5 年、20 億美元的合約，在紐約 Malta 幫 CoWoS 做矽中介層，2028 年上半年開始放量。
 
中介層就是 GPU 跟 HBM 坐的那片矽板。台積電把最緊的那一段，分一塊給別人做。
魏哲家在法說會上被問到這筆合作，原話是：
"Definitely, we have a little bit shortage on the back end, and we'd like to work with our so-called partner with GlobalFoundries."
法說會上他也講了：5 倍光罩尺寸已經量產，良率很好；9 倍、14 倍在開發；客戶的首選還是 CoWoS。
板子越做越大，一片晶圓切得出來的中介層就越少。台積電找了人一起扛。
台積電自己也沒停。這次法說它說，全球有將近 20 座廠同時在推，未來幾年在台灣要蓋 13 座先進製程和先進封裝廠，海外另外 5 到 6 座。今年資本支出 600 到 640 億美元，10 月法說會上重申不變（7 月講過其中一到兩成給先進封裝、測試、光罩這些）。
一家說「只有一點短缺」的公司，同時在蓋十幾座廠，還把一段工作外包到紐約。我讀起來，是缺口大到自己蓋不夠快。
輝達這週付的是頭期款
10/21，輝達在 GTC Berlin 一口氣公布一串供應鏈合約：
Amkor：南韓再加 13 億美元，連同先前的亞利桑那，多年協議（含預付款）合計 30 億美元；南韓目標 2028 年底中介層晶圓產能增加超過 300%。
京元電：11 億美元「產能保留預付款」，蓋美國測試廠，2027 年 4 月量產。
載板：揖斐電、三星電機、欣興，三年內輝達可用的載板產能合計拉到 2.5 倍。
矽品：CPO 光引擎產能，2027 年中拉到 15 倍。
 

有寫出金額的加起來：Amkor 30 億＋京元電 11 億，41 億美元，其中這週新增的是 Amkor 南韓 13 億＋京元電 11 億＝24 億，Amkor 亞利桑那那段是之前就簽的。揖斐電那筆只寫「數十億美元」（今年稍早已公布），還沒算進去。
 
這就像搶預售屋。房子還是一張設計圖，你先把頭期款匯過去，建商才肯幫你留那一戶。
麻煩的是交屋日期。京元電美國廠 2027 年 4 月。欣興新產能 2027 年第二季才開始加，2028 年中才滿載。格芯 2028 上半年。Amkor 2028 年底。
 

黃仁勳在同一份新聞稿講得更直接：「需求非比尋常，產能才是限制。」
瓶頸搬去哪
第一站，載板。
Google TPU v9 裡聯發科設計的 HumuFish 改走英特爾 EMIB-T（博通設計的 WhaleFish 還是 CoWoS-L），大家說台積電 CoWoS 被搶單。但 KeyBanc 估，EMIB-T 載板良率揖斐電約 50–60%、欣興只有 20–30%。這是分析師估計，不是公司公布。
TrendForce 10/22 引述天下雜誌和業界消息，第三季 EMIB-T 載板良率約 35%（年底目標 50%），但供應鏈說 HumuFish 仍「100%」用 EMIB-T。
35% 是什麼意思？你要 100 片好板，得投將近 286 片下去。
 

英特爾拿到的是門票，產能還要等良率爬上來。
第二站，機台。
Besi 今年前九個月的混合鍵合訂單，已經是 2025 全年的兩倍以上，客戶 23 家，累計需求超過 215 台。
 
那股價為什麼腰斬？一個是 SemiAnalysis 說 ASML 可能在做對手機台（ASML 沒證實，Besi 執行長說 ASML 不是對手）；另一個是市場擔心記憶體廠 HBM 導入混合鍵合會比較慢（執行長在法說也承認導入「有點延後」，但說開發沒停）。
還有一個原因比較少人講：Besi 說第四季營收大概跟第三季持平，上下 5%。訂單已經進來，機台還沒出貨，營收要晚幾季才跟上。股價看下一季，訂單看明後年。
第三站，測試。 輝達自己說，測試產能 2026 到 2027 要翻倍。
接下來我會盯的三個數字
台積電下一次法說：「有一點短缺」會不會又變回「瓶頸」。
EMIB-T 載板良率，從 35% 爬到 50–60% 要多久。
Besi 第四季訂單：公司說訂單動能會延續到第四季。
非投資建議，只是我自己的研究筆記。（我持有欣興）

Expert Takeaways: TSMC

1. CoWoS Capacity, Fab Breakdown, Spill‑Over Orders & Customer Allocation

Capacity Expansion: TSMC's internal CoWoS monthly capacity is targeted to reach 130k wafers by end-2026, with a long-term goal of 260k wafers/month by 2028 (excluding OSAT volumes).

Demand Growth: Market demand for CoWoS has increased by at least 26% compared to early-2026 levels.

Fab Breakdown: AP8 full capacity is 50k wafers (>40k expected by end-2026); AP7-P1 reached its 35k full-load target after ramping in August; AP7-P2 focuses primarily on SoIC; US AP1 will not ramp significantly by year-end; legacy AP1–AP6 fabs handle the remaining volume.

Expansion Bottlenecks: New packaging fab construction takes about three years from groundbreaking to bottleneck-limited full output, constrained mainly by hybrid bonding and 3–4 nm-grade CMP flatness requirements.

OSAT Spill-Over Strategy: Lower-margin orders are routed to external OSATs (ASE, SPIL, Amkor) under signed LTAs, reserving TSMC’s internal capacity for high-value customers.

Customer Allocation Split: Nvidia (60%), Broadcom (15%), AMD (10%), Marvell (6%), AWS in-house silicon (5%), MediaTek (2%), and others (3%).

2. SoIC Capacity Roadmap, Capital Intensity, Fab Bottlenecks & End‑Use Drivers

Capacity Roadmap: Targeted at 15k wafers/month by end-2026, 24–28k by end-2027, and up to 45k by end-2028 (~90% CAGR in 2027).

Capital Intensity & Bottlenecks: Capital intensity is $6.8–7.0 billion per 10k monthly wafers. Hybrid-bonding pick-and-place tools are the initial bottleneck, shifting dynamically to PVD and PECVD.

Manufacturing Limits: High CMP flatness and particle cleanliness requirements create a hardware ceiling below CoWoS scale. Capacity is concentrated at Chiayi AP7 through end-2027 (long-term potential 40–50k/month). US AP1 will take future volume but faces a long learning curve requiring Taiwan team transfer.

Key Demand Drivers: Nvidia (Rubin Ultra / Feynman), AMD (MI400 / Venice), Apple (M5 Pro / Max), and Broadcom ASICs slated for 2027.

3. Competitive Landscape (Intel / Samsung), Yields & Risk Mitigation

Intel EMIB-T Status: Yield estimates vary from ~90% (supply chain) to 38–40% (test-vehicle data). EMIB-T die cost is ~50% of CoWoS-L. Intel outsources all backend assembly to Amkor across Longtan, Portugal, and Arizona.

Samsung & Competitor Scale: Samsung I-Cube yield maturity lags peers, with meaningful competitive threats unlikely until post-2030 when hybrid bonding matures. Overall, TSMC’s advanced packaging volume is ~5× that of Intel.

Customer De-Risking: Google is validating EMIB-T as a backup due to TSMC tightness, costs, and US policy. Broadcom is evaluating EMIB-T and Samsung capacity, while building a joint substrate/FC-BGA facility in Singapore with Toppan.

4. CoPoS Technical Bottlenecks, Production Timeline & Silicon Utilization

Realistic Timeline: Mass CoPoS production in 2027–2028 is overly optimistic. AP7 has started qualification, aiming for limited NPI in 2027, low-volume production (LVM) for Nvidia Feynman in H2-2028, and true high-volume manufacturing (HVM) in 2029–2030. Glass-core TGV technology is deferred to post-2030.

Technical Challenges: Five core bottlenecks include substrate warpage, fine-pitch RDL lithography, coat-and-plate uniformity, ~70% copper-fill yield for TGV vias, and large-format panel-tool standardization.

Fab Footprint & Wafer Efficiency: US AP2 is provisionally planned for CoPoS. CoPoS requires greenfield fabs and won't cannibalize CoWoS. For large die sizes (e.g., 75×75 mm), CoPoS panel utilization reaches >84%, compared to just 48% on 12-inch circular wafers.

5. TSMC Co-Development Model & CPO Technology Outlook

Deep Joint Development: Advanced packaging is not off-the-shelf; TSMC collaborates closely with key customers on architecture, process flow, equipment limits, photomasks, and probe cards (e.g., scaling SpaceX probe sites from 4–6 up to 32up).

CPO Reality: Co-Packaged Optics (CPO) is not inherently tied to glass and can be built on silicon stacks. Key factors for success are I/O alignment precision and yield parity with CoWoS. Glass-based CPO currently faces high warpage and fracture risks.

6. Capital Expenditure, HPC Exposure & OSAT Dynamics

CapEx Upside: TSMC total capex guidance was revised up from $52–56B to $60–64B, with ~10% allocated to backend packaging (CoWoS/SooS).

Revenue Exposure: High Performance Computing (HPC) accounted for 68% of TSMC's Q3 revenue.

OSAT Role: External OSAT capacity serves purely as supplementary volume and cannot replace TSMC’s core leadership in high-end advanced packaging.

7. New-Fab Constraints, Capacity Methodology & Portfolio Strategy

Capacity Definition: Advanced-packaging fab capacity is defined by dynamic bottleneck tool stations (lithography, develop, die-bond, hybrid-bond) rather than physical floor space, creating variable output profiles across fabs.

A9/A10 & Future Fabs: Insider visibility on A9/A10 schedules remains limited with no firm dates.

Strategy: TSMC routes low-margin work externally while shifting internal capital toward next-gen CoPoS. Hybrid bonding and CMP flatness will remain recurring bottlenecks as Nvidia Feynman and HBM4-E ramp.

8. Supply-Chain Frictions from Constrained CoWoS-S Capacity

CoWoS-S Shortages: Shifted focus toward CoWoS-L has left CoWoS-S expansion constrained, weighing on 2026 customer deliveries.

Impacted Programs: TPU v7 / v8t implementations relying on CoWoS-S continue to face supply headwinds.

Alternative Approaches: Broadcom’s Sunfish uses CoWoS-L and is positioned well for 2027. Broadcom v8t and Humu-fish evaluated EMIB-T as an alternative, but yields remain inadequate, keeping supply pressure high on CoWoS-S programs.

欧洲的意外死亡与欧美渐行渐远的灰暗未来
欧美关系渐行渐远始于巴尔干危机，面对南斯拉夫的危机，欧洲求助美国帮助，欧洲人不仅不感恩，还对美国施下的种种道德陷阱，指手画脚。不过，如今的大分裂不只是军事与外交，更是塑造政治国家的深层因素：价值的危机。
美国副总统JD Vance抨击欧洲的衰落和种种倒行逆施时说：
“德国的整个国防开支都由美国纳税人补贴。成千上万的美军驻扎在那里。你觉得如果因为人们在推特上发表刻薄言论就把他们关进监狱，我们会容忍这种情况吗？友谊需要共同的价值观。如果你因为边境问题就把人关进监狱，因为选举结果取消选举，或者压制自己的人民，那我们之间就谈不上真正的友谊。”。
显而易见的说，欧美主流文明正处于危险之中，这一次的巨大危机却并非来自那个显而易见的敌人：苏联恶霸，而是来自欧美文明内部的更强大的敌人：灵性与道德的衰亡。那些在欧洲已经爆发的思想与道德病毒也潜伏在美国的思想、文化和社会核心，它如今正在威胁和终结主流文明。
这种威胁起初来自文艺复兴改革、法国大革命和俄国革命等世界历史性巨变所滋生的文化和精神病毒。诸如：唯名论、法国启蒙运动、实证主义、虚无主义、法西斯主义、马克思列宁主义和后现代主义等思想运动，它正在从内部腐蚀着西方文明。
文明危机主要并非政治危机，而是造成政治危机的那些根源性的要素：信仰和价值观的危机。因此，仅仅进行政治上的修修补补或经济上的调整并不能消除这些危机。文明并非由物质构成，它并非图书馆、教堂、城市或立法机构本身，这些只是文明的外在表现。
塑造欧美主流的文明的根源是关于人与神、与他人、与自我以及与自然的关系。背叛这种关系带来的是人对上帝的责任丧失，个人道德危机，社会开始腐化。
正是上述这些缘故，欧洲发生了可悲的文明自杀，欧洲的自杀有以下特征：
一、大规模移民
特别是2015年后德国总理默克尔主导的难民危机带来的海量异质文化的移民。这些移民与欧洲极低的本土生育率结合，正在迅速改变欧洲的人口结构，许多城市和地区本土欧洲人已成少数或即将成为少数。
举五个栗子：
1、布鲁塞尔（Brussels，比利时）：外国出生人口占比约47.9%（2023年数据，Statbel统计）。
2、阿姆斯特丹（Amsterdam，荷兰）：外国出生人口占比约37.1%（2023年数据，CBS统计）。
3、法兰克福（Frankfurt，德国）：非欧盟外国公民占比约29%（2019年数据）。
4、日内瓦（Geneva，瑞士） 与 苏黎世（Zurich，瑞士）：外国出生人口占比约40%左右。
5、伦敦（London，英国）：外国出生人口占比约37-40%（2021普查数据约37%）。
二、欧洲人对自身文明失去了信心
二次大战后，欧洲产生了对纳粹历史和殖民历史的强烈愧疚感，这种愧疚感如今演化成对西方传统和价值的系统性否定。因此，在接受大量异质文化的移民时，欧洲并不要求同化这些移民，甚至高举这些异质文化，否定自身，这是一种系统性自杀行为。
三、多元文化主义
对西方传统和价值观的系统性否定紧接着而来是多元文化主义，欧洲社会拒绝承认文化之间并不平等，恰恰相反，他们鼓吹性别平等、世俗主义、环保主义、多元文化平等、进步主义，这些思想与行动严重腐蚀了欧洲文明自身。
四、伊斯兰教在欧洲的快速扩张
在欧洲已经存在大量的伊斯兰国中之国的平行社会、伊斯兰社群设置的禁区、频繁发生的恐怖袭击、大量的强奸等，穆斯林移民社区与主流社会文化隔离、社区隔离、价值观隔离，这在欧洲形成了很多令人畏惧的文化马赛克社群。
五、政治精英的背叛
欧洲政治精英长期掩盖移民问题的规模和后果，压制批评声音，将任何质疑者贴上“种族主义”标签，导致民众对整个政治体系失去信任。可悲的是，由于大量进步主义选民的存在，这类糟糕的政客却总是能霸占政治话语权。
譬如，安格拉·默克尔（Angela Merkel）（2015年U-turn）的“开放大门”政策，让上百万穆斯林难民涌入德国，深刻改变了德国的人口结构。
巴基斯坦裔穆斯林团伙系统性虐待1400多名本土女孩长达十年以上，但警方、社会工作者和政客因害怕被指“种族主义”而延迟调查和行动。
德国科隆（Cologne）2015/2016年新年夜发生上千起涉及移民的强奸和抢劫案，然而，德国媒体和当局却压制报道，避免影响移民形象。
瑞典拥有全球最高强奸率，几乎全部由穆斯林移民犯下，但精英们压制统计数据和讨论，称其为“文化误解”。
上述的政治灾难背后的文化精神癌症还有以下几点：
1、同性恋：原本同性恋权利运动已基本胜利，取得同性婚姻合法化。然而，但运动并未停止，反而转向更激进的方向：取消文化，任何对同性恋的批评皆被视为”恐同症“。
2、女性权利、女权主义与性别问题。激进跨性别意识形态正在侵蚀女性权利，如女子体育、监狱、更衣室的安全与隐私，并压制科学讨论和女性声音。原先女权主义者已经不过进步，跨性别意识形态是当下欧洲的主流。
3、种族问题。反种族主义极端化，产生反“白人特权”原罪论、系统性种族主义等荒谬理论制造了新的种族对立。
4、社交媒体把少数激进声音放大成“多数共识”，制造虚假的道德恐慌。
大量移民带来的人口置换和主题文化的自卑与急剧衰落，正在掐死欧洲。
欧洲的衰亡带来了与美国关系的渐行渐远。
欧洲在全球GDP中所占份额持续下降；欧洲1.39的生育率不可持续，人口不断减少、老龄化，养育成本不断增加。欧洲超过10%的常住人口是外国出生的，约4500万人。然而，与没有阶级的美国不同，欧洲并没有美国式悠久的大熔炉式同化、融合和文化适应的传统。
与美国以基督教国家为主的移民模式不同，欧洲移民主要来自中东和北非，信奉伊斯兰教，并且越来越反西方。穆斯林移民无意融入他们认为颓废的欧洲文化，他们更倾向于征服欧洲。
基督教教会是西方文明的基石，如今的欧洲，无神论、不可知论以及对基督教的公开敌意，在欧洲极为盛行。
更可悲的是，欧洲实际上已经解除武装，他们没有能力保护自己的边界或利益。
欧洲在二次大战后大幅裁军、取消征兵、军费长期低于GDP 2%，军队装备老化、训练不足、战斗力虚弱。“福利国家寄生虫政策”，把保命的国防钱全砸到高福利、社会保障、绿色转型上，却指望美国纳税人出钱出力来保护他们。
欧洲对化石燃料的过度监管和打击，透支未来的社会福利制度，在进一步遏制欧洲经济的发展加速欧洲的衰亡。
当美国人指出欧洲的问题：放的边境、未融入主流社会的移民、部落主义、生育率下降、环保狂热、不可持续的预算赤字和巨额国债，这些欧洲病也开始威胁美国。但与欧洲不一样的地方在于，数百万美国人在巨大危机面前正积极行动起来，阻止美国的衰落。与此相反，欧洲人不仅拒绝美国这股保守、传统的拯救力量，还选择和他们背道而驰。
